title: Instrumentation calendar and triage rotations notes
content:
Goal:
Organize a lightweight, repeatable instrumentation calendar and oncall triage rotation for observability work that balances proactive metric hygiene with fast incident turnarounds. This doc is a working draft for the observability squad and adjacent owners (serving-runtime, platform-eng, product).

Summary / tl;dr:
- Weekly: short triage sync (30m) to review new alerts, metric churn, dashboard cost spikes.
- Monthly: instrumentation sprint window — prioritize pruning, sampling policy reviews, probe rebalancing, and dashboard slimming.
- Quarterly: retention and trace tier review, ownership refresh, and large-scale metric deprecation.
- Maintain a small roster (2 primary, 2 backup) for weekly triage; rotate monthly for primary ownership.

Why this now:
- Metric proliferation increased query costs and alert fatigue (see last quarter billing spike).
- Several recent rollouts (quantized-rollouts, dedicated-capacity) produced noisy probes that need a grooming cadence.

Weekly cadence (operational):
- Owners: rotation_roster.csv (keepshift list) — see PR#89 for automation.
- Meeting: Monday 10:30-11:00AM PT, triage sync.
- Agenda template: 5m highlights from oncall, 10m new alerts & proposed actions, 10m dashboard query-cost anomalies, 5m blockers/TODOs.
- Deliverable: update weekly triage ticket in JIRA-OBS board with actions and owners.

Monthly instrumentation sprint (2-day window):
- Schedule: chosen in the first week; aim for low-traffic weekend if possible.
- Focus areas: metric pruning (remove unused metrics), adapt sampling rates for traces, re-baseline SLI quantiles, and compactify heavy dashboards.
- Roles: sprint lead (observability), executor (serving-runtime infra), QA (console/product), comms (customer-success).
- Checklist: see "Monthly Sprint Checklist" below.

Quarterly review (policy + retention):
- Retention bands: 30d high-res metrics, 365d low-res aggregates, 7d trace full retention (configurable per-customer on Private).
- Budget review: present query cost delta + proposed rollbacks to finance.
- Owners refresh: reconcile ownership roster with team changes and oncall availability.

Monthly Sprint Checklist (working):
- Inventory: run metric-usage SQL (last 90d) -> top 200 queries by cost.
- Candidate prune list: metrics with <5 queries in 90d and not gated by rollout flags.
- Alert triage: mark alerts that fired >3 times in 7 days for suppression/re-tuning.
- Trace sampling sweep: propose target rates per service (see Trace Sampling table).
- Dashboard slimming: identify panels with >5s median query time or >$0.02 per refresh.
- Deploy rules to feature-flagged dashboards first for A/B.

Metric definitions (compact reference):
- inference.request.count | total inference requests accepted by the runtime | owner: eng-serving-runtime | unit: count
- inference.token.emitted | tokens emitted (response) | owner: eng-serving-runtime | unit: tokens
- kvcache.hit_rate | proportion of requests served from KV cache | owner: serving-runtime/kvcache | unit: ratio
- model.load.time.p99 | p99 model load latency (cold) | owner: platform-engineering | unit: ms
- tenant.slo.errors | rate of responses considered SLO failures by product criteria | owner: product-hosted-api | unit: percent
- dashboard.query.cost.estimate | estimated $ per dashboard refresh (derived) | owner: eng-observability | unit: dollars

(Notes: above fields are asked to be instrumented as stable metric names. If you already have similar names, add compatibility tags and alias mapping.)

Trace sampling proposals (draft):
- Baseline sampling: 0.5% full-traces global for long tails by default.
- Service-critical: 10% for serving-runtime critical path (kv lookup, compilation, serving-core).
- Error-weighted: sample 100% of traces that include status >=500 or contain alert tags.
- Adaptive bursts: increase sampling to 100% for 15 minutes when a critical alert fires (auto rollback after incident).
- Implementation sketch: use a central sampling service that accepts weights per-tag/service via a config API (INSTR-121).

Dashboard maintenance notes (pruning + UX):
- Naming convention: prefix dashboards with product-area/team (e.g., obs/serving-runtime/*).
- Tile limits: prefer 12 tiles per dashboard; panels beyond 12 must be split into a follow-on dashboard.
- Cost guardrail: dashboards with monthly refresh cost > $40 require a scheduled review.
- Realtime vs synthetic: separate dashboards for synthetic probes (low-cardinality) and realtime investigation (session slice capability).

Oncall + rotation guidelines:
- Weekly triage roster: two weeklies (Primary, Secondary). Primary handles meeting and ticket updates. Secondary stands up if Primary is OOO.
- Monthly rotation: primaries rotate on the first Monday of each month.
- Escalation ladder: primary -> secondary -> SRE lead -> eng director.
- Handover note template: last week hits, active suppressions, ongoing pruning tickets, blockers. Keep pinned in roster Slack channel.

Automation ideas (short list):
- Auto-ticket generator: scan for new alerts with >2 unique sessions and create draft JIRA-OBS items.
- Dashboard cost bot: annotate dashboards in the explorer UI with estimated cost and owner.
- Metric-use heatmap: nightly job that writes to a lightweight index for the monthly prune pass.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we centralize sampling config in the control plane (simpler ops) vs keep per-cluster control (more flexible for Private)? Pros/cons table TODO.
- How aggressively should we prune metrics produced by customer-managed Private deployments? Need legal/CS check (audit logs requirement).
- Where to store rotation_roster.csv (GH repo vs Drive)? Proposal: keep canonical roster in private repo (infra-config) and export to Drive for visibility.

Immediate action items (this sprint):
- Maya: prototype metric-use heatmap job (WIP branch, PR#89).
- Jonah: add monthly sprint calendar invite template and tentative windows for Q1 2026.
- Priya: draft trace-sampling config API spec and link to INSTR-121.
- Ethan: run dashboard cost scan and produce top 20 dashboards by estimated monthly cost.

Notes to self / style fragments (working brain dump):
- Keep triage meetings short and action-oriented. No rehash of old incidents — use incident timeline if needed.
- Build small guardrails rather than heavy-handed blocking (we don't want to slow model rollouts).
- Communication: publish sprint summaries in #ops-observability and tag impacted product owners.

Reference artifacts / useful queries (links & starters):
- Metric-usage SQL: SELECT metric_name, count(*) as queries, sum(cost) as cost FROM metric_query_logs WHERE ts > now() - interval '90 days' GROUP BY metric_name ORDER BY cost DESC LIMIT 500;
- Dashboard-cost estimator: internal script in gh: observability/tools/dashboard-cost-estimator
- Related Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/c/OBS-Runbook-Calendar

Version history / decision log:
- 2025-11-15: created (initial draft)
- 2025-12-02: added weekly cadence and sprint checklist (input from Jonah)
- 2026-01-10: appended trace sampling proposals and open questions (Priya)

If you are reviewing: leave comments inline or add follow-up items to JIRA-OBS-482. For immediate sync, ping @obs-squad in Slack and attach this doc.

-- end of draft --
